A famous castle in the North East has appeared on a list of haunted wedding venues in the run up to Halloween 2026

11:23, 26 Oct 2026Updated 14:48, 26 Oct 2026

It's a place many couple have sad 'I do' and this year hosted its first ever music festival. And now, in the run up to Halloween, a very famous castle in the North East has officially been ranked as one of the UK's most haunted wedding venues, with sports stars who once stayed there so spoked that they checked out early.

‌

‌

With the clocks going back in the early hours of Sunday and, us facing two storms in a matter of days in the shape of Austen and Boelo, summer now feels like a distant memory and, although it feels like Christmas is very much just around the corner, let's not forget that Halloween is up first. And, if you fancy enjoying some luxurious but ever so slightly eery surroundings to mark the occasion, you' may want to head to County Durham landmark Lumley Castle.

‌

The castle near Chester-le-Street has made it the top 10 most haunted places to tie the knot in the UK, joining the likes of Hampton Court Palace and Warwick Castle in the list compiled by wedding experts Bridebook. Lumley Castle, dating back to the 14th century, is home to the ghost of Lily of Lumley, the wife of Sir Ralph Lumley who was thrown down a well in the castle grounds by two priests after she rejected the Catholic faith.

‌

Her ghost is said to rise from the well and drift through the castle walls. Lumley Castle overlooks Durham cricket ground, meaning its had its fair share of famous guests over the years. The story goes that three West Indies players were so unnerved that they checked out early, while India captain Sourav Ganguly later recalled fleeing his room during India's 2002 tour and, in 2005, Australian all-rounder Shane Watson famously spent the night on teammate Brett Lee's floor after being spooked in his room.

‌

Speaking about the castle in 2009, Watson told press: "I didn't see anything, but it was a very spooky sort of place and it definitely freaked me out - things that probably aren't there but some people believe are there. People go there to actually see the ghosts."

Lumley Castle is leaning into its haunted reputation next month with an event called Spooked, described as an 'immersive evening of unimaginable mystery and magic.' Guests are invited to journey through a series of eerie rooms where strange experiments, ghostly encounters, and impossible illusions await around every corner.
